To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned the gene encoding the second galanin receptor subtype and have shown that it has a wide tissue distribution and mediates a wide range of biological activities in human cells in vitro.

We have isolated and characterized a human gene encoding the galanin receptor subtype GALR2 and have demonstrated that this receptor couples both to G alpha q/11 to stimulate PLC and increase intracellular Ca2+ levels and to G alpha i/o to inhibit forskolins-stimulated intracelluar cAMP accumulation.
we have isolated the cDNA encoding the human GALR 2 galanin receptors and have shown that the receptor is expressed widely in both the central nervous system and peripheral tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and characterization of the gene and protein encoding human GALR1, GALR2 and GALR3, the three galanin receptor subtypes.
the molecular and cellular biology of the galanin receptor subtypes and the identification of novel ligands for the galanin receptors.
the cloning and characterization of the human GALRN2 gene and receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GALR2 galanine receptor is a member of the G protein-coupling receptor family and is expressed in many human tissues.
GALR2 is an important galanin receptor subtype that mediates a diverse array of biological activities in the central and peripheral nervous systems.
the GALNR2 gene encodes the second galanin receptor in humans and that this receptor couples to multiple G proteins and is expressed in a wide spectrum of human tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned, characterized and localized the human galanin receptor 2 (GALR2) and that it has a wide distribution throughout the body.
we have cloned a novel galanin receptor that is highly expressed in many tissues and is coupled to both phospholipase-C and adenylyl-cyclase pathways.
human GALR2 is a functional receptor that mediates the biological actions of galanin and that it has a widespread tissue distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
human GALR2 is a functional G protein-coupling receptor with a broad tissue distribution and that the GALNR2 gene is localized to chromosome 7q25.
the human GALR1 and GALR2 galanine receptors are highly similar to each other and to other members of the G protein-coupling receptor family, and that they are widely expressed throughout the body.
the human GALNR1 gene is located at 17q25, whereas the GALNR2 gene is located at chromosome 17q21-q22.
